export const meta = {
  name: 'globe-writers-1',
  description: 'Write the evidence-only README sections as fragments: verified sources + street-zoom/design references, rendering options, pipeline/cost + predeclared evaluation',
  phases: [{ title: 'Write fragments', detail: 'three section writers in parallel' }],
}

const REPO = '/home/user/RoofingApp'
const EVID = REPO + '/research/globe/validation-evidence/'
const FRAG = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86e0a23e7a7/scratchpad/readme-sections/'

const CTX = `You are a section writer for research/globe/README.md, the single reference document for the "3D storm view" (globe) research in RoofingApp. A supervisor assembles the sections; write ONLY your fragment file, in Markdown, nothing else.

Context you must read first: ${EVID}main-architecture.json (the product is now the Montana Hail Watch WEBSITE — static pages built every 10 minutes by GitHub Actions and published on Pages; the browser may fetch only site files; third-party code is vendored, never a CDN; phones first; the 24 "what the globe plan must change" points), ${REPO}/research/globe/README.md sections 1-7 (the original plan, written for the parked desktop app; its evidence rules in section 4 stand, its constraints are superseded), the scratchpad supervisor log at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/*/scratchpad/supervisor-log.md (find it with ls; read the verdict sections), and the evidence files named in your task. In every evidence file a "review" key (the independent refuter's corrections) WINS over "facts"; where a file has no review, say "unreviewed" next to the number.

House style (the owner's): plain wording, sentence case, direct, brief; tables and ranked lists over prose; a number always carries its unit and its source as a link to the evidence file, e.g. [mrms.json](validation-evidence/mrms.json), or "computed: <formula>"; anything the evidence did not verify is written "unverified" with why; no "best" claims about any provider or library (AGENTS.md rule 9); evidence honesty wording (rule 5): observation / satellite estimate / radar estimate / official alert, never damage, "no echo is not clear", MRMS -99 and -999 are "no radar data (meanings unverified)", cloud-top height is an estimate of the top only; the site's gap words ("No radar coverage", "No model data", "Outside map area", "This is not an all-clear."). Never write model names or AI-vendor identifiers. Do not repeat section 1-7 material; cross-reference it. Headings: use the exact section numbers and titles given in your task (## N. Title), subsections ###. Keep your fragment at or under the line budget given. Write the file at the path given (create the directory if needed). Return as your final text: the fragment path, its line count, the list of evidence files you cited, and any fact you found contradicted between files (file A says X, file B says Y).`

const S8 = `# Fragment: sections 8 and 13 → ${FRAG}08-sources.md (budget 220 lines)
Evidence: ${EVID}gibs.json, goes-aws.json, mrms.json, radar-tiles.json, terrain.json, base-imagery.json, labels-on-globe.json, montana-imagery-buildings.json, design-references.json, google-terms.json, rights-matrix.json, parallax.json, prior-work.json.
## 8. Verified sources
Open with two sentences: what was checked (live request + content decoded, then an independent refuter) and the date. Then one table per group — Clouds (GIBS GOES layers; GOES on AWS: ACHAC 10 km and ACHA2KMC 2 km, CMIPC band 13, CODC), Storms (MRMS 3D levels, composite, MESH; NEXRAD Level II; NWS radar services; NCEP GeoServer; IEM tiles), Earth (terrain tiles, 3DEP; base imagery: USGS retired on main, GIBS Blue Marble/VIIRS, Natural Earth + Census as the site's base; Esri and Sentinel-2 terms), Labels (USGS Imagery Topo, GIBS reference layers, OSM policies, CARTO, MapLibre-style vector tiles, Apple MapKit JS as a candidate) — columns: source · what it is (kind) · cadence · measured latency · bytes per step or tile · grid/resolution · licence (short) · hostable by the site? · browser-fetchable today? (no — site files only; say what rule would change) · evidence. Then "### Corrections the refuters made" (the important ones: two cloud-top products; GIBS declared vs served tile levels and 19–96 min latency; MRMS has no coverage-mask product, -999 is the only coverage signal, levels are MSL, 19.8–24.9 MB per 2-min step; IEM/NWS public-domain wording limits; MSL imagery retiring 2026-07-31; terrain 952 m check) and "### Still unverified" (MRMS -99/-999 meanings, GIBS parallax status, satellite GeoColor source, Cesium ion commercial terms reading, etc.). Then "### Parallax" with the measured table summary and the two legend wordings from parallax.json (quote them verbatim) and the GOES-East grid longitude note (-75.0 grid vs -75.2 nominal, ~0.14 km).
## 13. Design references and street zoom
The owner's six screenshots (research/globe/design-references/01…06, zoom bands with corrected zoom estimates), what each band needs and which free source covers it, what has no source yet (3D buildings, POIs, district shading), the Apple terms note (no screenshot clause; legal notices must stay visible), the OSM Boundary Extractor as a boundary importer (open question: export format), the Montana street-zoom sources (MSL NAIP 2025 ~0.3 m placeholder, 2019–2023 0.6 m, retirement date; USGS tiles LOD 16 ~1.6 m; Overture/Microsoft footprints with licences; TIGER/OSM boundaries), and the honesty note that street-zoom imagery is a base map, never a storm-timed roof record.`

const S9 = `# Fragment: section 9a → ${FRAG}09a-rendering.md (budget 140 lines)
Evidence: ${EVID}rendering-options.json, globe-libs.json, webgl-runtime.json, prototype-globe.json, prototype-mrms.json, prototype-goes.json, parallax.json, mrms.json.
## 9. How to draw clouds and storms
### 9a. Rendering techniques
A table of the techniques (draped texture; cloud deck displaced by cloud-top height; volumetric ray-marching in a 3D texture; sparse voxel points/boxes from MRMS — what the prototype draws; isosurfaces at display classes 20/35/50 dBZ; stacked translucent slabs; 2D fallback) with columns: data needed · computed where (build job vs browser) · bytes per frame for the Montana frame box (formula) · GPU/memory class with reason (MAX_3D_TEXTURE_SIZE 2048 from webgl-runtime.json) · what it honestly shows and its legend text · failure modes (MSL levels below ground; parallax; no-data cells; frame gaps; interpolation = false precision, forbidden) · phone fit · phase. Then "### Library capabilities" — a comparison table from globe-libs.json (CesiumJS 1.146, MapLibre GL JS 5, three.js/globe.gl, deck.gl + pydeck): vendored bytes, licence, WebGL version, time-dynamic imagery, 3D textures/volumes, terrain without an account, map tiling, Python wrapper — no ranking, no "best". Then "### What the prototype showed" in five lines (voxel counts and draw results from prototype-globe.json and prototype-mrms.json; the flat-blob note at 1x exaggeration; the Cesium ion credit note). End with "### Existing viewers" (3–5 public viewers that draw GOES or radar in 3D, each with its data source sentence and URL from rendering-options.json).`

const S10 = `# Fragment: sections 10 and 12 → ${FRAG}10-pipeline.md (budget 200 lines)
Evidence: ${EVID}pipeline-options.json, hosting-options.json, main-architecture.json, mrms.json, goes-aws.json, prototype-mrms.json, prototype-goes.json, evaluation-predeclared.json.
## 10. Data pipeline and cost
Start from the fact that the site already has the job: website.yml builds every 10 minutes within 15 minutes, from empty, downloading 45.7 MB and writing 3.9 MB per live build (main-architecture.json). Table of options: (A) add the globe's products to that build; (B) a second scheduled job (why website.yml's single-publisher model makes this hard); (C) a small always-on server (prices from hosting-options.json; roadmap item 8 context); (D) on each visitor's device (not possible for GRIB/netCDF in a browser — say so). Per option: bytes per build (GOES frame, cloud-top PNG for ACHAC vs ACHA2KMC, MRMS volume crop at 20 and 35 dBZ, terrain once), minutes added to the job (from measured decode/download times), bytes per visitor per page view and per 10-minute refresh, monthly Pages bandwidth at a stated visitor count (formula), $/month, latency to the page (10-minute build means 10–20 minutes behind the source — quote DECISIONS:354-355 via main-architecture.json), failure surfacing (problem/stale states, page-age banner), privacy (statewide products only; no place lists), what --previous must carry for a loop. Then "### GitHub Actions facts" (5-minute minimum, drops under load, default branch only, 60-day pause, the Actions terms sentences — note once that the site already relies on this and the owner may want a legal reading), "### The frame-bytes budget" with numbers and derivation (the earlier plan's Phase 3 cited a budget that did not exist — give it here), and "### Product format" (compact JSON vs binary + sidecar, sizes).
## 12. Predeclared evaluation
From evaluation-predeclared.json: purpose (fidelity of the rendering to its source and comprehension of labels — not hail accuracy), the 16 metrics in a table (name · definition · pass rule), the fidelity checks, the held-out cases table (dates, counts, sizes, URLs; why 2025-06-15 is excluded), the SPC day rule, the comprehension test, "What this evaluation does not claim", data needed. Keep every number and date exactly as the file has them.`

log('Writing evidence-only README fragments: sources+street zoom, rendering, pipeline+evaluation')
const out = await parallel([
  () => agent(CTX + '\n\n' + S8, { label: 'write:08-sources', phase: 'Write fragments', model: WORKER }),
  () => agent(CTX + '\n\n' + S9, { label: 'write:09a-rendering', phase: 'Write fragments', model: WORKER }),
  () => agent(CTX + '\n\n' + S10, { label: 'write:10-pipeline', phase: 'Write fragments', model: WORKER }),
])
return { fragments: out }

Fragment: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad/readme-sections/08-sources.md

Lines: 185 (budget 220). Covers "## 8. Verified sources" (Clouds, Storms, Earth, Labels, Corrections the refuters made, Still unverified, Parallax) and "## 13. Design references and street zoom" (the six screenshots, zoom bands, no source yet, Apple terms, OSM Boundary Extractor, Montana street-zoom sources, honesty note, corrections). Links resolve; no model or vendor names; no emoji.

Evidence cited (validation-evidence/ unless noted): gibs.json, goes-aws.json, mrms.json, radar-tiles.json, terrain.json, base-imagery.json, labels-on-globe.json, montana-imagery-buildings.json, design-references.json, google-terms.json, rights-matrix.json, parallax.json (no review key, marked unreviewed), prior-work.json, main-architecture.json; design-references/01 to 06 JPEGs (viewed directly). rights-matrix.json also has no review key and is marked where its figures are its own.

Not read directly: globe-libs.json (its "up to three hours" figure is taken from rights-matrix.json); prototype-goes.json and prototype-mrms.json (the P3 note comes from the supervisor log).

Contradictions between files (A says X; B says Y):
1. README §4: "MRMS carries its own no-coverage mask". mrms.json: no coverage-mask product exists; -999 is the only coverage signal.
2. mrms.json: -99 and -999 are "no radar data (meanings unverified)". sources.py:116 and gridded.py:192 (per rights-matrix.json): negative MRMS values are called "no radar coverage".
3. gibs.json: the NASA map-library page says "the time parameter is not supported". The same file's live KVP request with TIME returns frames.
4. gibs.json: layer limits say GeoColor level 6 and Band 13 level 5. The server serves 7 and 6 over Montana.
5. radar-tiles.json: NWS MapServer says "Update Frequency: Every 5 minutes". Observed CONUS record gaps reached 8.27 min, and 12.7 min unless an unpolled record existed.
6. radar-tiles.json: IEM shows 149 px opaque over Billings at 03:18 UTC; NWS WMS and NCEP show 0 px in the same window. QC explanation plausible, not proven.
7. goes-aws.json: NODD says NOAA data are "open to the public and can be used as desired". The files' global attribute says "Access is restricted to approved users only". data.gov lists ACHA as CC0 but non-public.
8. montana-imagery-buildings.json: Microsoft's README says CDLA Permissive 2.0; Overture lists the same footprints under ODbL.
9. montana-imagery-buildings.json: the MSL state page says NAIP 2025 is 30 cm; the service's pixelSizeX 0.3 is in Web Mercator units, about 0.205 m on the ground at 47 N (computed).
10. goes-aws.json: GOES-19 subpoint -75.2 (file attribute). Supervisor-log P3 note: GOES-East grid origin -75.0 (prototype-goes.json). parallax.json uses -75.2. Effect about 0.14 km.
11. google-terms.json: root tileset valid "at least three hours". rights-matrix.json (quoting globe-libs.json): "up to three hours".
12. README §3 cites D12 for GOES 15 min and MRMS 10 min. prior-work.json: D12 holds radar 15, alerts 10, SPC 60, forecast 12 h; GOES and MRMS limits are proposals.
13. README §4: "tens of km poleward". parallax.json: the shift is away from the satellite (NW for GOES-East, NE for GOES-West); "tens of km" only for tops around 12 km and up.
14. README §4: "GIBS imagery is not parallax corrected". gibs.json: unverified (zero shift on 5 frames; cloud-height effect untested).
15. design-references.json: USGS imagery (D9) covers the street bands, and state borders are "none in s3". main-architecture.json: USGS tiles are retired (D28), and basemap.json draws borders and labels.
16. design-references.json: keep the dark storm look (D19; base.html tokens). main-architecture.json: dark mode is a system setting only (style.css tokens). The suggestion predates D27–D28.
17. base-imagery.json: services.arcgisonline.com returns HTTP 200 with no token; basemaps-api and ibasemaps-api return HTTP 200 with error 499 "Token Required". Ambiguous rather than false; the pricing page names only the billed hosts.
18. terrain.json: the joerd README says terrarium "creates tiled output in GeoTIFF format"; the S3 terrarium objects are PNG.

Fragment path: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad/readme-sections/09a-rendering.md

Line count: 80 (budget 140). It opens with "## 9. How to draw clouds and storms" and "### 9a. Rendering techniques", then has the Library capabilities, What the prototype showed and Existing viewers subsections, in that order.

Evidence cited (all in validation-evidence/): main-architecture.json, rendering-options.json, globe-libs.json, webgl-runtime.json, prototype-globe.json, prototype-mrms.json, prototype-goes.json, parallax.json, mrms.json, globe-volume.png. Also referenced only through those files: gibs.json, goes-aws.json, terrain.json. The supervisor log supplied the Cesium ion credit note, and the fragment marks it as not in an evidence file.

Contradictions between files:
1. Radar freshness: prototype-globe.json uses 15 min for the radar layer and 10 min for the MRMS volume layer (both marked proposals). main-architecture.json says the site code uses 30 min (gridded.py:53), and its doc_drift item 1 says DESIGN.md and DECISIONS.md say 15 min.
2. Frame box: rendering-options.json uses the prototype plan box (lon -116.8 to -103.3, lat 43.6 to 49.75, 1,350 x 615 cells per level). main-architecture.json gridded.crop uses lat 43.0 to 50.5, lon -118.5 to -101.0, which is 1,312,500 cells per level (computed), 1.58 times larger. The fragment uses the plan box and states the factor.
3. Browser fetch: rendering-options.json technique a has the browser fetch GIBS tiles. main-architecture.json plan point 19 says the browser may fetch only site files. The fragment makes the fetch a build-time step.
4. Fallback layer: rendering-options.json technique g uses the NWS base reflectivity WMS (D7). main-architecture.json plan point 9 replaces it with the site's MRMS PrecipRate frames. Both drafts are shown.
5. MapLibre version: the task brief says "MapLibre GL JS 5". globe-libs.json measured 6.14.0, and the globe projection arrived in 5.0.0. The fragment uses 6.14.0.
6. Chromium version: globe-libs.json says its browser run used headless Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (Playwright 1.64.0). The webgl-runtime.json review says only chromium-1194 (141.0.7390.37) was installed and headless_shell-1248 was missing. prototype-globe.json and rendering-options.json say 141. Not resolved; the fragment cites 141 for the SwiftShader numbers.
7. MRMS negatives: mrms.json says -99 and -999 must not be labelled "no radar coverage" until verified. main-architecture.json says the site treats MRMS negatives as "no coverage" and uses the hatch word "No radar coverage" (map.js:33-39). Flagged in Table 2, row c.
8. Parallax: parallax.json assumes GOES-East at -75.2 and gives a legend of "20 to 33 km". prototype-goes.json reads the grid origin as -75.0 (Missoula 15 km: 33.628 km against 33.456 km), and rendering-options.json puts the upper bound near 34 km. parallax.json lists sea level versus ground as open; prototype-goes.json says the CF standard name answers it (geopotential, geoid-referenced), with the geoid offset not applied.
9. HT units: prototype-goes.json says metres (scale 0.3052). rendering-options.json records a NESDIS caption saying feet, unresolved.
10. Loop length: rendering-options.json's per-2-hour figures assume 60 frames at 2-minute steps. main-architecture.json says the site builds every 10 minutes, so a 2-hour loop has 12 frames at build cadence (computed in 9a).

Identical copy: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad/readme-sections/10-pipeline.md (the task's directory did not exist, so I created it and also wrote the copy to the session scratchpad path, which the supervisor log says is the real one; `cmp` confirms they match).

Lines: 198 (budget 200). Sections: "## 10. Data pipeline and cost" and "## 12. Predeclared evaluation", with the three required subsections under 10.

Evidence files cited (all in validation-evidence/): pipeline-options.json, hosting-options.json, main-architecture.json, mrms.json, goes-aws.json, prototype-mrms.json, prototype-goes.json, evaluation-predeclared.json, terrain.json (linked for the terrain row only; its sizes are not summed).
Repo checks: docs/DECISIONS.md:354-355 quote verified verbatim; docs/ROADMAP.md item lines; .github/workflows/website.yml (cron 15, concurrency 31-33, build timeout 38, upload 157, deploy needs build 162, deploy timeout 165).

Contradictions and drift (file A says X; file B says Y):
1. evaluation-predeclared.json (decision_time_leaks) uses 35–99 s source latency; mrms.json's review refutes that as a general range (whole day 2026-10-16: 29–120 s).
2. evaluation-predeclared.json says goes-aws.json shows 0 objects dated 2026 and newest ACHAC 2025/097; the current goes-aws.json gives 0 for GOES-16 only, with 290 day folders each for GOES-19 and GOES-18.
3. ROADMAP numbering: the evaluation cites item 3 as the evaluation baseline and item 4 as the Benchland example. docs/ROADMAP.md has item 3 = Company limits, item 4 = decision-time records (review P0 baseline), and Benchland in item 11 (lines 69-71). hosting-options.json and pipeline-options.json cite item 8 for "Phone/SMS/email delivery needs a small always-on service" (desktop-era ROADMAP:87-88). In the current file, item 8 is the text version of the map, and item 12 (lines 74-75) says "Needs a small service" with no "always-on" wording. §10 uses item 12.
4. Decode peak RSS: pipeline-options.json says 363.6 MB; prototype-mrms.json says 409 MB (both all 33 levels, different measurement). §10 gives both.
5. Radar stale limit: the evaluation's 22-min "Stale" fixture assumes D12's 15 min. The code uses 30 min (website/gridded.py:53; sources.py:115), DESIGN.md:154 and DECISIONS.md:341 say 15, and DESIGN.md:333 says 30. As coded, the fixture would not test the site's boundary. Listed as §12 conflict 1.
6. Places and time zone: the evaluation's data_needed uses the desktop app database (store.py). main-architecture.json says the site has 14 towns, no saved places, and Montana-time labels.
7. Frame budget box: the prototype box (1,350 × 615 at 0.01°, about 82.8 square degrees) differs from the site frame box (43.0–50.5 N, 118.5–101.0 W, website/gridded.py:38, about 131.3 square degrees, 1.6 times larger). The 1.0 MB budget needs re-measuring on the site box; §10 says so.
8. ROADMAP.md:50 says each build downloads "about 40 MB"; the measured figure is 45,673,824 B (main-architecture.json). §10 uses the measured figure.
9. GOES HT units: the evaluation cites a NESDIS caption in feet; prototype-goes.json reads the file attribute as metres (scale 0.3052037). Resolved in favour of the file attribute.
10. GOES-East longitude: parallax.json assumed −75.2; prototype-goes.json reads −75.0 as the grid origin (−75.2 is the nominal platform subpoint), effect at most 0.17 km. Not used in these sections.

Notes for assembly:
- evaluation-predeclared.json is not edited, per its frozen-version rule; §12 lists the conflicts for a new version.
- Items for the owner or counsel, not legal advice: the GitHub Actions terms (the existing site already relies on them), NOAA attribution, the GOES "Access is restricted" banner, and the Pages commercial-use sentence.
- Flagged as unverified in the text: ACHA2KMC crop size, the 35 and 50 dBZ binary sizes (estimates), CI decode time (sandbox only), the 9,000-views-a-month assumption (from hosting-options.json), and terrain sizes.
- No repository file was changed.
